text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chief Justice of the Federal Court Eusoff Chin has advised lower courts to impose a minimum one-week jail sentence on those who are guilty of committing serious offences.
- Tan Chee Khoon, better known as Mr. Opposition among Malaysians, died at his home today (Sunday). He was 77.
- Several rivers in the Cameron Highlands district are fast becoming illegal 'dumping grounds' for flower growers and farmers.
- Bank Negara Malaysia is not easing on credit restraint. In fact, it is expected to continue with the policy of restraint for quite a while more.

- The country's largest cooperative, KUB Malaysia Bhd, upon its successful listing on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, is expected to record a market capitalisation of 2.14 billion ringgit at a price earnings ratio of 20.
